cards.headline: Ukraine evacuates 167 civilians from Kherson region as Oleshky ceasefire nears expiry

pages.text: Ukraine’s military evacuated 167 people from threatened areas of the southern Kherson region as a temporary local ceasefire neared its end. The evacuation, conducted by civil-military cooperation units of the “South” group of forces in coordination with local authorities, included 22 children and 21 people with limited mobility requiring special assistance, according to the Ukraine General Staff on Telegram. This movement occurred two days after busloads of residents were brought out of the Russian-held town of Oleshky, which had been under Russian occupation for four years. The six-day local ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding area was scheduled to expire at midnight Moscow time (2100 GMT) on October 25, 2026. It represented the longest local pause in fighting since the full-scale Russian invasion began in 2022.

cards.headline: Nine people killed in Learjet crash in South Florida residential neighborhood

pages.text: Nine people died on November 1, 2026, when a Learjet 60 business jet crashed into a residential neighborhood in South Florida, United States. U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy described the incident as a “horrific tragedy” in a post on X, stating that everyone on board was killed in the crash. The aircraft was traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when the accident occurred. Austin-Bergstrom International Airport confirmed the aircraft was a private jet but did not provide the identities of those on board. Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the crash as “cataclysmic,” telling reporters the plane “looked like a missile going down” and left a large crater on the side of the road. While the plane appeared to fall just meters from homes and cars, DeSantis stated there appeared to be no casualties on the ground.

Cockpit recordings retained by LiveATC.net captured the final moments of the flight. The pilot was heard discussing “manageable” ice issues before later stating the plane was rapidly losing altitude. Shortly after, the panicked crew said, “We’re going to crash into the ground.” Online videos of the incident appear to show the jet striking the ground at a high speed and a sharp angle, followed by a large explosion. Footage of the aftermath shows flames flickering around debris and chunks of pavement as people milled around the area. Federal Aviation Administration staff were en route to the crash site to support an investigation by the National Transportation Safety Board.

cards.headline: University of Cambridge researcher among those killed in Spanish high-speed train crash

pages.text: Dr. Marta Shahbazi, an award-winning researcher at the University of Cambridge, was among the 69 people killed when a high-speed train crashed into a stationary train near Urda, south of Madrid, on October 28, 2026. Shahbazi was traveling to her native Spain to collect a Spanish Society for Developmental Biology award at a conference in El Rompido, Andalusia, when the collision occurred. The crash, which involved a state-operated Renfe high-speed train hitting a stationary Iryo company train, is one of the worst rail disasters in modern European history and Spain's worst crash since 2013. Authorities in the Castile-La Mancha region announced on October 31, 2026, that 36 fatalities had been conclusively identified following autopsies at the Institute of Forensic Medicine in Toledo. As of that date, 66 of the 69 people killed had been identified, including 54 Spanish nationals and 12 internationals. Local authorities reported that the three remaining unidentified victims are believed to be foreign nationals, including one Japanese national and two Australians.

Dr. Shahbazi was an affiliate associate professor and a principal investigator at the University of Cambridge's Stem Cell Institute (CSCI). She also led a research group at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) on the Cambridge Biomedical Campus, where she ran the Shahbazi Laboratory. Her research focused on cell biology and the earliest steps of human embryo development, specifically how errors in these processes can lead to failed pregnancies. The LMB described her as an inspiring and talented scientist, noting she was a role model for the term she used for herself, a 'mother scientist,' as she worked to balance her career with raising two young children. Prof. Bertie Gottgens, director of the CSCI, stated the community was shocked by the loss of a researcher highly respected for her pioneering work and collaborative spirit. Shahbazi had joined the Cambridge laboratory in 2020 after completing her PhD at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre.

The investigation into the collision is focusing on the failure of the LZB train protection system and possible decision-making errors at the Madrid railway control centre. Media reports have published radio recordings suggesting the Renfe train driver was instructed by a staff member at the Madrid control centre to resume normal operations while the LZB system was out of service and the other train remained on the track. Regarding the approximately 200 injured passengers, Castile-La Mancha regional president Emiliano García-Page stated on October 31, 2026, that 34 people were still receiving treatment in four hospitals, with 15 in intensive care. He noted their conditions were improving relatively well. The railway line between Madrid and Andalusia remains closed in both directions.

cards.headline: 2,000 Salvadoran troops deployed to Haiti following disappearance of four technicians

pages.text: A convoy of heavily armed Salvadoran troops, including soldiers carrying automatic weapons and new armored vehicles, was seen in the Tabarre neighborhood of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, on October 30, 2026. The convoy is part of a deployment of 2,000 troops sent by El Salvador President Nayib Bukele to the country. This deployment follows a gang attack on four Salvadoran members of the Gang Suppression Force, who have gone missing. The Haitian government stated the four individuals were abducted. President Bukele wrote on X that El Salvador “only wants to bring home the four missing aviation technicians.” Writing in Haitian Creole, Bukele stated, “This is not an operation against the Haitian people, nor an invasion of the country of Haiti,” adding that El Salvador is not a great power and has no interest in dominating the Haitian people or seizing Haiti’s wealth.

The Haitian government issued a statement saying the two nations are reinforcing cooperation within the framework of the U.N.-backed gang suppression force. However, experts have questioned the specific role the Salvadoran troops will play and whether the move will lead to an escalation of violence. While no group has claimed responsibility for the attack on the technicians, social media in Haiti featured videos of gang leaders defying President Bukele and promising to “outgun” his troops. According to the U.N., more than 5,700 people were killed or wounded in Haiti between January and mid-September.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo kills more than 5,000 people

pages.text: The death toll from an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000, according to government data released on October 30, 2026. The epidemic, which was declared in mid-May, has infected more than 10,000 people and is the country's deadliest on record. Figures from the Congolese Ministry of Health showed 5,026 people have died among 10,351 confirmed and suspected cases, resulting in a fatality rate of nearly 50%. The BBC reported the case fatality rate is 48.6%.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species, a rare strain of the Ebola virus for which there are currently no approved vaccines or specific treatments. While clinical trials are underway, health workers are providing supportive care based on patient symptoms. Ebola is a deadly disease that spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids, such as blood or vomit, and can lead to vomiting, diarrhea, organ failure, and in some cases, internal and external bleeding. The United Nations has warned that the current outbreak is taking lives at a much faster rate than previous ones.

The virus has spread to 67 of the country's 178 health zones across eight of its 26 provinces. The epidemic is concentrated in eastern Congo, specifically in the Ituri and North Kivu provinces, which have recorded a combined 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. The Ministry of Health identified the Ituri province, located in the north-east of the country, as the epicenter. The region is a conflict zone, which officials say makes it harder to contain the virus. Additionally, some health workers and a politician have been attacked while responding to the outbreak.

uncertainties: The exact number of deaths and cases varies slightly between sources: the Ministry of Health reported 5,026 deaths among 10,351 cases, while other reports cite more than 10,300 confirmed cases and more than 5,000 deaths.

cards.headline: Thousands rally in New Delhi to demand resignation of India’s election chief

pages.text: Thousands of protesters marched through New Delhi to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstration, led by Indian National Congress party leader Rahul Gandhi, follows more than a month of protests challenging the revision of electoral rolls and the conduct of the election chief. Demonstrators marched from central New Delhi toward the Ramlila Maidan ground, waving Indian and party flags while opposition leaders traveled in an open-top jeep. Officials implemented traffic diversions and increased security measures ahead of the march. Around the rally site, hundreds of police officers, some equipped with shields and batons, were deployed alongside riot-control vehicles.

The protests center on a revision of voter lists that removed more than 130 million names. Opposition parties allege this exercise disproportionately affected Muslims and other minorities considered unlikely to support Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The opposition claims these changes favor the BJP. The Election Commission has denied favoring any party, stating that voters whose names were wrongly removed may register again. The BJP has accused opposition parties of undermining democracy by challenging electoral procedures. Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda dismissed the demonstration as a “carefully orchestrated drama.” India’s next general election is due in 2029.

cards.headline: Garment workers block Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur, Bangladesh

pages.text: Garment workers staged a protest on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in the Kaliakair upazila of Gazipur, demanding that the minimum monthly wage be raised to Tk 30,000. The blockade, which began at 7:00am in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area, caused traffic congestion stretching at least 10km on both sides of the highway. Traffic eventually returned to normal after approximately six hours of disruption. At least 30 factories declared holidays during the daylong protests, road blockades, and violence. Earlier protests had also occurred in Safipur Bazar, Mouchak, and Telichala within Kaliakair.

Authorities deployed 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel and executive magistrates to control the movement of workers, according to Gazipur Deputy Commissioner Md Nurul Karim Bhuiyan. Kaliakair Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shahidul Islam stated that efforts were underway to resolve the situation through talks with the workers. Islam claimed that a group of workers and outsiders had gathered in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area to block the highway and launch the demonstration. Police also noted allegations that outsiders had joined the workers' movement to instigate unrest. Around 12:30pm, a police van and a fabric scrap (jhut) warehouse belonging to a garment factory were set on fire in the Chandra Palli Bidyut area, causing panic before law enforcement personnel brought the situation under control.

cards.headline: Serbian police official arrested for suspected abuse of office

pages.text: Marko Kricak, the head of Serbia's criminal police directorate, has been arrested and charged with abuse of office, according to state media reports. The 42-year-old is accused of suppressing and manipulating an investigation into the May murder of a suspected criminal underworld figure in a Belgrade restaurant. Kricak, who was appointed commander of the Serbian police's personal protection unit (JZO) in July 2023, was a former car salesman recruited into Serbia's domestic intelligence agency, the BIA. He was considered a loyal supporter of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) and defeated President Aleksandar Vucic. Belgrade's chief prosecutor, Nenad Stefanovic, told journalists that the arrest has no link to the results of the legislative elections. However, the arrest follows the October 25 parliamentary elections, in which Vucic's right-wing populist camp was defeated by the opposition Student List. The removal of Kricak and other Vucic loyalists from the police and intelligence apparatus was a specific demand made by student leaders. Kricak has also faced accusations from student groups regarding police brutality during peaceful anti-Vucic demonstrations. While prosecutors deny a connection to the election, the arrest of a senior officer regarded as close to the former regime is being viewed by some as an indication that strongholds of the Vucic system are slowly eroding.

cards.headline: Shops looted and clashes erupt during cost-of-living protests in Germany

pages.text: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt and clashed with police late on October 31, 2026, as demonstrations over the cost of living turned violent across several German cities. While thousands participated in largely peaceful demonstrations earlier in the day, violence broke out in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. In Frankfurt, police closed off a large section of the main shopping street overnight and reported making many arrests. In other cities, police used water cannons to disperse protesters who were targeting emergency workers with stones, bottles, and fireworks.

The demonstrations were organized by the campaign group Gen Z regelt—which means “Gen Z takes charge”—to protest against military service, public spending cuts, the high cost of living, and underfunding in schools. Lina Friedrich, a spokesperson for Gen Z regelt, stated the demonstrations were intended to fight for peace and freedom rather than war and coercion, emphasizing support for health and education systems and opposition to compulsory military service. Authorities in Frankfurt, Munich, and Berlin reported as many as 18,000 protesters, a figure that represents roughly half of the organizers' estimate. German media reported that tens of thousands protested in German cities on October 31, 2026.

Germany's Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told Bild newspaper that overnight police had prevented violence similar to that seen in Paris in recent weeks, and he called for harsh punishments for looters and rioters. The unrest in Germany follows youth-led mass protests in France, where more than 320,000 people also demonstrated on October 31, 2026.

cards.headline: Arab-Israeli coalition leader says Israel has 'historic' opportunity to oust Netanyahu

pages.text: Yousef Jabareen, leader of Israel’s main Palestinian coalition, said the country faces a historic opportunity to change direction following recent elections. Jabareen, who heads the Joint List, stated he is ready to join forces with the “Change” bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition to wrest control of the Knesset, Israel's parliament. The Arab-Israeli parties currently hold the balance of power in the 120-seat legislature after winning a record 19 seats. The Joint List holds 11 seats, while the more conservative, Islamist Ra’am party holds eight seats. This follows a significant shift in voter behavior, as turnout among Arab Israelis—Palestinians with Israeli citizenship who make up approximately 20% of the population—more than doubled to about 80%. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza did not vote.

The political landscape has shifted as Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority, dropping from 68 to 53 seats. The “Change” bloc of Zionist parties, led by retired general Gadi Eisenkot, holds 48 seats. Because no single grouping commands a clear claim on power, Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, is expected to summon political leaders to canvass recommendations on who should be given the first chance to form the next government. Jabareen told the Guardian that the primary demand of the roughly 840,000 Palestinian Israeli voters is to remove the Netanyahu government, specifically targeting national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and finance minister Bezalel Smotrich.

Jabareen described the previous four years as an “awful” and “very dangerous period” for the Arab community. He cited several issues, including house demolitions, a lack of police intervention regarding criminal gangs within the Arab community, and insufficient resource allocation for municipalities, education, and youth. He also noted racism in various areas of life, including physical attacks against Arabs and police brutality. Jabareen indicated that the next few days will be critical for the country's political direction.

cards.headline: Negotiators braced for worst during US-Iran talks to reopen Strait of Hormuz

pages.text: Officials from Gulf states are “braced for the worst” as indirect negotiations in Doha, Qatar, continue regarding a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The talks involve the United States and Iran and aim to address the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets, which could lead to the reopening of the waterway and the restart of negotiations on Iran’s nuclear programme. Gulf officials are awaiting a response from Washington to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait before the US midterm elections on October 27, 2026.

To address a lack of trust between the two nations, Qatar is attempting to negotiate a plan to compress the timeline for diplomatic actions. Under this proposed plan, the US would lift sanctions, followed by Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and beginning nuclear talks. Iran has agreed to reduce the timetable for this process from seven days to two days. Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi stated that there are currently no plans for direct talks with Washington, though he said Iran is ready for both diplomacy and defence depending on the “rationality” of the US.

The mediation efforts continue following an incident on October 30, 2026, when unidentified missiles struck a Qatari LNG tanker bound for Pakistan near the Strait of Hormuz. The attack occurred despite the ship having received direct clearance and safe-passage approval from Tehran just hours earlier. United Arab Emirates envoy Anwar Gargash said that another round of escalation is not in the interests of Iran or its neighbours, noting that relations with Iran are essential to avoid a prolonged crisis.

cards.headline: Wage protests spark clashes and factory closures in Bangladesh

pages.text: Garment workers in Bangladesh engaged in protests demanding higher wages on November 1, 2026, leading to clashes, arson, and highway blockades in Dhaka, its outskirts, and Gazipur. The unrest occurred on the same day the government formed a new wage board. According to a situation report from the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), at least 529 garment factories in Mirpur, Savar, Ashulia, Gazipur, and Mymensingh declared a holiday by the evening of November 1, 2026. The workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000, the reinstatement of dismissed employees, and an end to blacklisting. The previous minimum wage increase, which moved the rate from Tk 8,000 to Tk 12,500, took effect on December 1, 2023.

In Dhaka, several hundred ready-made garment (RMG) workers blocked roads in Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11, and Mirpur-14 starting around 9:00am. Clashes occurred around 11:45am when police attempted to disperse the demonstrators, resulting in chases and the exchange of brick chunks. The unrest caused the closure of the Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11, and Pallabi metro stations for approximately two hours. During the protests, a police vehicle was set on fire in Mirpur-11. In Savar, demonstrators torched a security booth at a garment factory, and fires were reported at several locations in Gazipur, including a factory warehouse.

Police detained 30 people in Mirpur, alleging that activists and leaders of the Awami League—a political party whose activities are banned—and its affiliated bodies were exploiting the worker protests. Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury also alleged that various political organisations were instigating workers to cause public suffering and destabilise the government.

cards.headline: Police disperse garment workers attempting to take to the streets in Mirpur, Bangladesh

pages.text: Garment factory workers made scattered attempts to take to the streets through various alleys in Mirpur, Bangladesh, on November 2, 2026, leading to confrontations with police. In the Senpara Parbata area of Mirpur-10, workers tried to emerge onto the main road through an alley at approximately 10:45 am. Police responded by chasing the group and firing several tear gas shells to disperse them. The workers later moved away from that area. Later, at approximately 11:00 am, workers also tried to take to the streets in the Proshika intersection area beside the stadium in Mirpur-2. Eyewitnesses reported that workers were arriving in small, scattered groups from the Rupnagar area, passing the stadium toward the intersection, before police obstructed them and drove them away.

Following two consecutive days of protests and clashes involving garment workers in Mirpur, law enforcement agencies have been on alert. Police personnel were deployed around the Mirpur-10 roundabout and nearby areas from early morning on November 2, 2026, with riot-control vehicles and water cannons kept ready. Despite the tension, traffic in and around Mirpur-10 was moving normally, and the situation appeared normal at approximately 10:30 am. Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Joint Commissioner (Crime Prevention–North) Mohidul Islam stated that police are investigating whether individuals are seeking to create disorder, disrupt public safety, or conspire to damage state property. Mohidul Islam also noted that an investigation is underway to identify those involved in clashes and an attack on a police vehicle, adding that investigations have found the involvement of other criminals alongside the workers.

cards.headline: Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu discuss potential combat operations against Iran

pages.text: US President Donald Trump held a call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on October 31, 2026, to discuss whether to increase combat operations against Iran, according to reports from US media. The discussion focused on the timing of potential strikes and the current state of negotiations with the Islamic republic. Axios, citing one US official and one Israeli official, reported that Netanyahu pressed Trump to launch strikes on Iran immediately following the US midterm elections, while Trump expressed a desire to allow negotiations to proceed. An Israeli source described the call as “tough,” while an American source characterized it as “direct.”

The call occurred during an eight-month war in which Trump has pursued two simultaneous strategies with Tehran: conducting a campaign of airstrikes and other attacks, while attempting to reach a deal to initiate peace talks and fully open the Strait of Hormuz to oil and gas traffic. On October 31, 2026, Trump told reporters that negotiations to end the war were “going fine,” though he noted there were still one or two targets to “take care” of. He stated that Washington was not in a hurry to take offensive action, asserting that the US had already decimated Iran’s nuclear program and military. These discussions followed a disclosure by Iran’s security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, that he had received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance regarding the revival of stalled talks. Trump has faced political pressure from US midterm voters concerned about rising gas prices and cost-of-living increases.

cards.headline: Jordan designates Hmoud as City of Culture for 2027

pages.text: Jordan has named the village of Hmoud, located in the Karak governorate, as the country's City of Culture for 2027. Culture Minister Mustafa Rawashdeh announced the designation, which aims to emphasize national unity and solidarity following a mass shooting attack on a Christian community in the village that killed at least nine people. Rawashdeh stated the recognition honors the village's place in national memory and the residents' contributions to education and culture. The decision is intended to reaffirm the role of culture in promoting social cohesion, citizenship, and tolerance.

To support the designation, the ministry will establish a library, a cultural street, a memorial to commemorate the village's history, and the Hmoud Prize for Arabic Fiction. During a visit to Hmoud, Rawashdeh reaffirmed the ministry's commitment to a national vision led by King Abdullah II to preserve national identity, expand access to knowledge, and promote mutual respect and moderation. Fares Halasa, president of the Hmoud Heritage Revival Association, welcomed the initiative on behalf of residents, stating it honors the village's history and reaffirms a commitment to coexistence, education, and national unity.

cards.headline: Bangladesh sends first batch of 12 workers to Mongolia

pages.text: A batch of 12 Bangladeshi migrant workers departed for Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, via China on the night of November 1, 2026, marking the first deployment of Bangladeshi workers to the East Asian country. The deployment was facilitated by the state-owned Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Ltd (BOESL) and represents an opening of the Mongolian job market to Bangladeshi manpower exports. According to BOESL, the 12 workers will be employed in warehouses and as support staff at shopping malls and markets. Mohammad Rashedul Haque, Managing Director of BOESL, stated that the agency provided pre-departure training to the workers and that the deployment reflects government efforts to find overseas employment destinations beyond traditional labor markets. Mr. Haque noted that Mongolia has a high demand for skilled workers across different sectors. Another 18 Bangladeshi workers are reportedly preparing to travel to Mongolia for employment shortly.

The 12 workers will receive a monthly salary of US$400 and a daily meal allowance of $4. The recruiting Mongolian company will also provide free accommodation. The workers will undergo an initial three-month probationary period, during which they will receive their salaries, meal allowances, and accommodation. Employment contracts are set for two years with an option for renewal, and Mr. Haque noted that contracts could be extended based on worker performance.

cards.headline: Pickering city council to return to in-person meetings on Nov. 16

pages.text: Pickering city council is scheduled to return to in-person meetings in its newly renovated council chambers on Nov. 16, following nearly two years of conducting municipal business online. The city previously shifted all council proceedings to a virtual format due to escalating security concerns, disruptions, and graphic threats related to the conduct of former councillor Lisa Robinson. Mayor Kevin Ashe described the move to online meetings as a ``prudent'' step to protect staff, council members, and residents, stating that people should feel safe in their place of government. Robinson, who lost the mayoral race to Ashe on October 26, 2026, was investigated nine times by the city’s integrity commissioner since 2023 and faced several pay suspensions ranging from 30 to 90 days.

The return to in-person meetings follows a $3.3 million renovation of the council chambers. While the upgrades were completed this summer, the council had not returned to an in-person format since moving online. Mayor Ashe characterized the upgrades as ``comprehensive,'' noting that no major structural or technological updates had been made to the chambers since the civic building opened in 1989. Maurice Brenner stated that a major focus of the overhaul was ensuring full accessibility under provincial standards. In response to the conduct of former councillor Robinson, Pickering councillors had previously petitioned the provincial government for legislation to create a standard code of conduct for all municipalities, which would allow for the removal and disqualification of members in serious violation of the code. The Ford government passed that legislation.

cards.headline: Money worries affect 72% of workers in Bangladesh, survey finds

pages.text: Financial stress is increasingly impacting employee productivity in Bangladesh, with 72 percent of workers reporting that money worries affect their performance, according to the 2026 Employee Benefit Trends Study by MetLife Bangladesh. This figure rose from 56 percent the previous year. The study, which surveyed 709 people including 583 employees and 126 employers, spanned several industries such as readymade garments, manufacturing, banking, insurance, telecommunications, retail, information technology, education, and non-governmental organisations. While financial concerns grew, job satisfaction improved, with 83 percent of employees reporting they were satisfied with their jobs, up from 78 percent in 2025. However, fewer employees expressed a willingness to recommend their organisations as good places to work.

The MetLife Bangladesh survey indicates a growing expectation for employers to assist with long-term financial security and unexpected expenses. In 2026, 86 percent of employees believed employers should help them save enough for retirement, an increase from 67 percent in 2025. Additionally, 81 percent of employees stated that employers are responsible for their financial wellbeing, compared to 69 percent a year earlier. These findings suggest that workers are increasingly looking for workplace benefits that extend beyond salaries and traditional perks to address broader financial stability.

cards.headline: Energy-efficient fans could reduce Bangladesh's peak power demand by up to 2,590 MW

pages.text: A study by the Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) found that replacing inefficient household fans in Bangladesh with brushless direct current (BLDC) models could reduce the country's peak power demand by up to 2,590 megawatts (MW). The report, titled ‘Household Space Cooling in Bangladesh: Role of Energy-Efficient Fans’, notes that household fans account for 5,212 MW of the country's summer power demand, with usage peaking around 9:00 pm. On August 27, 2026, the country's peak power demand reached 19,027 MW at 9:00 pm. High demand has at times led to load-shedding—the intentional shutdown of electric power in parts of a grid to prevent total failure—exceeding 3,500 MW.

The IEEFA report, authored by Shafiqul Alam, lead energy analyst for Bangladesh, states that BLDC fans consume 35 watts (W) compared to 70 W or more for inefficient models. Currently, BLDC fans account for only 1.4 per cent of fans in use. The study, which was based on a survey of 435 households across 26 districts, found that even low-income households use up to two fans during summer. The adoption of BLDC fans could save up to 6,913 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of electricity annually, valued at Tk 89.87 billion ($0.73 billion). Shafiqul Alam noted that global energy supply disruptions have made it harder for the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB) to meet demand, and wider adoption of efficient fans could ease pressure on the BPDB.

Beyond reducing summer demand, the IEEFA study suggests that replacing inefficient fans with BLDC models could help avoid more than $4 billion in future investment in coal-fired power plants. The report indicates that the savings in upfront capital expenditure would be sufficient to replace all inefficient fans currently in use across the country.

cards.headline: 72-year-old suspect arrested in Ashanti Region for Sakumono murders

pages.text: Police arrested 72-year-old Samuel Christopher Osei Anto at a hideout in Tikrom, near Ejisu in the Ashanti Region, on Sunday, November 1, 2026. Anto is a suspect in the killings of Irene Atubiga, 47, and her uncle, George Atubiga, 57, which occurred at their NTHC Estate residence in Sakumono, Greater Accra Region, on Friday, October 30, 2026. During the operation, police retrieved a Smith & Wesson pistol and seven rounds of live ammunition from Anto. The Ashanti Regional Police Command stated on Monday, November 2, 2026, that Anto is in custody to assist with investigations, and the recovered firearm and ammunition are being held as exhibits.

Preliminary investigations by the police suggest the murders resulted from a financial dispute between Anto and George Atubiga. According to the Ashanti Regional Police Command, Anto had allegedly borrowed GH¢500,000 from George but failed to repay the debt. An earlier police account noted that Anto had visited the victims' residence with Beatrice Mumuni, 47, to demand repayment before a misunderstanding allegedly escalated into the fatal shooting.

cards.headline: Western Australia facial recognition trial scans more than one million faces and results in 122 arrests

pages.text: A five-month trial of real-time facial recognition technology in Western Australia resulted in 122 arrests and nine incorrect alerts after scanning 1,380,882 faces. The trial, which concluded on October 31, 2026, involved 100 deployments of surveillance vans across 43 regional and metropolitan locations. In addition to the arrests, the technology led officers to engage with 146 registered sex offenders and locate 10 people for welfare checks. A police spokesperson confirmed the nine incorrect alerts represented an error rate of 0.00065% against the total scans. During a media conference on November 1, 2026, Western Australia police commissioner Col Blanch confirmed that officers engaged with each individual involved in the false alerts.

The trial included three operations at the Perth royal show. During these specific operations, 223,749 faces were scanned, which resulted in 15 alerts, three arrests, and seven interactions with registered sex offenders.

cards.headline: False emergency alerts issued in Ukraine and Russia following reported cyberattacks on alert applications

pages.text: Ukraine and Russia have both reported cyberattacks targeting applications used to send emergency alerts to the public. On November 1, 2026, a series of false emergency warnings were sent to users in Ukraine, beginning at approximately 22:47 (20:47 GMT) with red-level air raid alerts issued nationwide in Ukrainian. Subsequent false warnings specifically targeting Kyiv included a declared radiation threat, a Russian-language message stating there would be a nuclear alert across Ukraine due to the flight of an Oreshnik missile, a chemical threat, and a threat of street fighting. Oreshnik is a Russian intermediate-range ballistic missile capable of carrying either conventional or nuclear warheads. At 23:53, a series of all-clear messages were delivered to the phones that had received the Kyiv alerts, declaring each threat clear. While details regarding alerts sent in Russia are limited, a Ukrainian espionage group claimed that fake warnings of nuclear strikes were sent to users inside Russia.

cards.headline: Australian author Craig Silvey jailed for child exploitation material

pages.text: Australian novelist Craig Silvey was jailed for seven months after pleading guilty to possessing and distributing child exploitation material, a Western Australian district court heard. The 44-year-old author, known for the novel Jasper Jones, was found with numerous category one photos and videos on his mobile phone and laptop during a police raid of his Fremantle home. Judge Hayley Cormann described the offending as very serious, very disturbing, and devastating because it involves children.

cards.headline: Clashes erupt in Manipur, India, after five Kuki men were found dead

pages.text: Clashes have broken out in the Kangpokpi district of Manipur, India, following the recovery of the bodies of two Kuki men who had been missing for several days. The victims, identified as 20-year-old Paoginlal Hangsing and 20-year-old Tinginlun Chongloi, were recovered by a joint security operation and taken to the Kangpokpi District Hospital. Tensions escalated after their deaths were confirmed, leading to clashes in the district. The circumstances surrounding the clashes were not immediately clear, and the extent of casualties and damage was not immediately available, according to an NDTV report via bdnews24.com. The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) had previously called for a shutdown across the district following the disappearances of the two men.

The deaths in Kangpokpi occurred one day after three Kuki men were killed in a shootout between two unidentified groups in the state’s Noney district. In response to the unrest in Kangpokpi, security forces have increased efforts to restore order. As agitated demonstrators continued protests, police moved the bodies to the Kangpokpi superintendent of police’s office and law enforcers fired several rounds of tear gas shells to disperse the crowds.

cards.headline: 17-million-year-old fossil found in Egypt challenges theories of ape origins

pages.text: The discovery of a 17-to-18-million-year-old ape fossil in northern Egypt is challenging long-standing scientific theories regarding where the ancestors of modern apes, including humans, first evolved. The fossilized remains of the newly identified species, *Masripithecus moghraensis*, were recovered from Wadi Moghra, making it the first definitive fossil ape ever discovered in North Africa. This find suggests that the evolutionary lineage leading to all living apes may have emerged much farther north than previously believed, potentially placing northern Africa and the Middle East at the center of this evolutionary history. For decades, scientists believed early apes and their relatives were concentrated primarily in regions farther south in Africa. While fossil sites in North Africa have produced remains of ancient monkeys from the Early Miocene, researchers had not previously found definitive evidence of apes from that same period. Hesham Sallam, a paleontologist at Mansoura University and senior author of the study, stated that the team spent five years searching for this fossil because North Africa appeared to hold a missing piece in the early ape family tree.

cards.headline: Researchers realize anti-spin ice by using attracting particles

pages.text: Researchers reported the realization of an anti-spin ice, a system that breaks the rules governing conventional spin ices, in a recent Nature Communications study. While most studies of colloidal ices have used repulsive particles, this new research examined the effects of particles that attract each other instead. This creates an anti-spin ice that behaves in the opposite manner of traditional spin ices. Scientists recreate these behaviors in engineered systems called artificial spin ices, which are constructed from arrays of tiny magnets or microscopic particles known as colloids. In these colloidal ices, particles reside in tiny grooves, or wells, arranged along a lattice, with each particle resting near one end or the other of a groove.

Spin ices are magnetic systems that mimic the ice rule found in water ice. In water ice, each oxygen atom keeps two hydrogen atoms close and two hydrogen atoms farther away. Because many different arrangements can satisfy this rule equally well, the hydrogen atoms in ice remain disordered without a repeating pattern. This disorder is a sign of geometric frustration, a state occurring when competing interactions in a system cannot all be satisfied at once, resulting in many equally valid compromises. In typical colloidal ices, particles repel each other and spread out evenly to keep the imbalance of particles at each junction, known as its topological charge, as small as possible. The anti-spin ice realized in this study reverses this dynamic by using attracting particles.

cards.headline: Global human metabolism produces an estimated 2.05 billion metric tons of CO₂ annually

pages.text: A University of Bath-led study published in The Lancet Planetary Health estimates that the collective carbon dioxide produced by humans as their bodies convert food into energy reached 2.05 billion metric tons per year in 2015. This figure represents a 74% increase from 1.18 billion metric tons in 1985. Researchers found that population growth accounted for more than 60% of this increase, rather than a significant rise in the amount of CO₂ produced by each individual person. The study, led by Professor Javier Gonzalez of the University of Bath's Center for Exercise, Nutrition and Metabolism, used thousands of real-world measurements of CO₂ production from people ranging from infancy to old age, combined with global population and body-weight data. Scientists say these findings could help improve carbon accounting by providing a more accurate understanding of where carbon originates and how human activity fits into global carbon movements. The researchers noted that human metabolism is a sizable part of this movement, particularly in heavily populated towns and cities.

The researchers emphasized that the CO₂ produced through human breathing is not the same as emissions from burning fossil fuels. The carbon exhaled by people comes from the food they consume, which consists largely of carbon that plants have recently absorbed from the atmosphere. In contrast, fossil fuels release carbon that has been stored underground for millions of years. Professor Gonzalez stated that the study is not suggesting that breathing is driving climate change or that people should change their diets or exercise habits. Instead, the goal is to provide scientists with a more accurate piece of the puzzle to help predict how effective various carbon reduction strategies may be.

cards.headline: Induced inflammation temporarily increases anhedonia and reduces desire to socialize

pages.text: A randomized, placebo-controlled study published in Psychoneuroendocrinology found that experimentally inducing inflammation in healthy women temporarily increased symptoms of anhedonia and lowered their desire to socialize. Anhedonia is a reduced ability to feel pleasure or interest in activities that were previously enjoyable, such as hobbies or social interaction. While the inflammation had more limited effects on how the women responded to smiling faces, it impacted the motivation to seek social contact. The study was conducted by Chloe C. Boyle of the Norman Cousins Center for Psychoneuroimmunology at the University of California, Los Angeles, and colleagues to test how acute inflammation affects the processing of social rewards.

Researchers distinguish between two aspects of reward processing: “wanting,” which is the motivation to pursue something desirable, and “liking,” which is the pleasure experienced when receiving it. While previous studies suggest inflammation can reduce the motivation to pursue rewards, its effects on the actual experience of pleasure have been less consistent. This research is relevant to understanding depression, a leading cause of disability worldwide that affects emotional well-being and the ability to maintain social relationships. Although the causes of anhedonia are not fully understood, evidence suggests inflammation—a natural immune response to injury or infection—can influence how the brain processes emotions, motivation, and rewards.

cards.headline: Hubble and Webb telescopes find clues about early solar system in distant icy objects

pages.text: NASA's Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have uncovered clues about the earliest days of the solar system by examining some of the smallest and faintest objects observed beyond Neptune. By investigating trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs)—tiny bodies that orbit the Sun far beyond Neptune—astronomers have found evidence suggesting these distant, icy bodies have preserved information about their origins for billions of years. This discovery challenges existing expectations regarding how planets form. Most of these objects are extraordinarily difficult to detect, shining more than 100 million times more faintly than objects visible to the naked eye. For the first time, researchers combined observations from both Hubble and Webb to study these TNOs, identifying 27 previously unknown objects.

The findings, detailed in two related studies published in The Astronomical Journal, revealed an unexpected puzzle. Researchers found fewer small objects than some theories predicted, and the colors of these objects closely resembled those of much larger objects in the same distant regions. These frozen remnants provide a rare opportunity to study the materials that eventually became planets. Scientists believe planet formation began when tiny particles of dust and pebbles orbiting the young Sun gradually accumulated into larger bodies. Over time, these materials formed objects roughly the size of cities, known as planetesimals. While these early building blocks eventually combined to create the planets seen on November 2, 2026, that final stage of growth did not occur for many objects beyond Neptune.

cards.headline: Estrogen-only hormone therapy linked to fewer signs of Alzheimer’s disease in brain tissue

pages.text: Women who use estrogen-only hormone therapy during menopause may have a lower risk of developing the brain changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease, according to research published in the journal Neurology. A large analysis of patient data found that those who used the therapy had less physical evidence of the disease in their brains and better memory test scores. This study follows investigations into whether the natural decline of estrogen during menopause contributes to the fact that Alzheimer’s disease disproportionately affects women, who make up more than two thirds of all patients worldwide.

To understand the relationship between estrogen and brain health, Stanford University psychiatry and behavioral sciences researcher Jennifer L. Bruno and colleagues examined records from thousands of older women. Estrogen helps regulate physiological processes that keep the brain healthy, such as inflammation and the integrity of the blood-brain barrier. The blood-brain barrier is a cellular filter that shields the brain from harmful substances in the bloodstream.

The findings come after past research on whether menopausal hormone therapy helps protect against dementia yielded mixed results. Some trials suggested a protective effect, while others found either no benefit or an increased risk of cognitive decline. Researchers noted that variations in the timing of treatment, the specific chemical formulation used, and the genetic backgrounds of patients have made it difficult to draw a definitive conclusion.

cards.headline: Large physical movements can increase complex learning speeds by 4 to 6 times

pages.text: A study from Florida Atlantic University and Brown University found that physical movement dramatically assists with certain types of complex learning. Researchers explored how different levels of bodily motion affect the ability to process information using virtual reality (VR) gaming technology. In a laboratory setting, Luke Rosedahl, Ph.D., an assistant professor of Biomedical Engineering at Florida Atlantic University, and Isabella Cabaleiro, a research lab specialist, conducted an experiment where participants wore VR goggles to view various striped objects. The goal was for participants to learn how to categorize these stripes into specific groups as a game progressed.

The experiment compared different methods of responding to the stimuli. Some participants used small motions, such as pressing buttons, to categorize the stripes. Other participants used much larger motions, such as swinging a lightsaber to hit the stripes or punching a response box located in front of them. Rosedahl told NPR's Emily Kwong that the difference in learning outcomes was dramatic, noting that people using larger movements like punching learned somewhere between 4 and 6 times faster.
